seo_description: ShotClipSearch keeps every image and screenshot you copy and recognizes the text inside on your Mac, so you can search them. Free, open source, offline.
hero_sub: ShotClipSearch saves each image you copy and reads the text in it on-device. Press Command Shift V, type a word, and copy the right picture back.
features_sub: Everything runs locally, from capture to text recognition to search.

features.title: Image-first clipboard history
features.desc: Watches the clipboard for PNG, JPEG and TIFF images, including screenshots copied with Control Shift Command 4. Text copies are ignored.

features.title: On-device text recognition
features.desc: Apple Vision reads the text in each image in the background. Choose automatic detection or a specific language in Settings.

features.title: Search words, apps and dates
features.desc: The search field matches recognized text, the source app name and the date. Cards show the first line of text and a timestamp.

features.title: Keyboard-driven gallery
features.desc: Open it with Command Shift V, move with arrow keys, press Return to copy back, Space to preview and Delete to remove.

features.title: Retention you control
features.desc: Keep images for 7, 30 or 90 days, or forever, and cap storage between 50 and 1000 images. Pinned images never expire.

features.title: Private by design
features.desc: No server, account or network code. Images, thumbnails and the index stay in a folder on your disk. Transient pasteboard items are skipped.

permissions_step: No special permissions are required. If you turn on Launch at login, macOS lists the app under System Settings > General > Login Items.

faq.q: Is ShotClipSearch really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license and the full source is on GitHub. There are no accounts, subscriptions or paid tiers, and an optional Support button links to Ko-fi.
None. It only reads the clipboard, never captures your screen, and the global shortcut does not need Accessibility access. Launch at login is optional and appears in Login Items.
Images, thumbnails and a JSON index are kept in ~/Library/Application Support/ShotClipSearch/ on your Mac. Text recognition runs on-device and nothing is sent over the network.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to launch it, or build it yourself from source with Xcode and XcodeGen.
